report_name: AI-Assisted Campaign by GreyNoise13 Hits 22 Orgs via Check Point Flaws

threat_actors.name: GreyNoise13
threat_actors.description: A previously unknown threat actor, designated GT13, has been conducting a widespread and sophisticated campaign since at least October 17, 2026. The group targets Check Point Security Management servers using AI-driven tooling for automated exploitation and hands-on-keyboard activity for post-compromise actions.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor exploited multiple public-facing applications by leveraging a range of critical vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-16232 in Check Point SmartConsole, CVE-2025-5777 in Citrix Netscaler, and CVE-2024-21893 in Ivanti products for initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Network Service Discovery
attack_patterns.description: The actor used Nmap for internal reconnaissance to map the internal network after gaining initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Protocol Tunneling
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor used the Chisel tool to create secure tunnels for command and control and lateral movement.

attack_patterns.name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
attack_patterns.description: The actor utilized tools like Impacket to interact with Windows network protocols for lateral movement.

attack_patterns.name: Virtual Private Server
attack_patterns.description: The attackers utilized disposable servers and routed traffic through the ExpressVPN service as part of their operational infrastructure to obscure their origin.

tools.name: Nmap
tools.description: Used for internal network reconnaissance to map the internal network of compromised organizations.

tools.name: Impacket
tools.description: Used for interacting with Windows network protocols for lateral movement.

tools.name: Chisel
tools.description: Used to create secure tunnels for command and control and lateral movement.

tools.name: Paramiko
tools.description: Used for making SSH connections during post-exploitation activities.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-16232
vulnerabilities.description: A critical authentication bypass in Check Point SmartConsole that allows an attacker to gain administrative privileges, used for initial access.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2025-5777
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability in Citrix Netscaler exploited by GT13 for initial access.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2024-21893
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw in Ivanti products exploited by GT13 for initial access.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-41089
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability in Windows Netlogon exploited by GT13 for initial access.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-61500
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability in Rejetto HFS (HTTP File Server) which was exploited to use a compromised server as a relay.

identities.name: Organizations in Critical Sectors
identities.description: A group of at least 22 organizations across the energy, transportation, financial services, and government sectors compromised by GreyNoise13.

infrastructure.name: GT13 C2 Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Operational infrastructure consisting of 99 IP addresses, including disposable servers and egress nodes routed through the ExpressVPN service to obscure their origin.

infrastructure.name: GT13 Operational Relay
infrastructure.description: A compromised server, vulnerable to CVE-2026-61500 (Rejetto HFS), was repurposed by the attackers to act as an operational relay for C2 and data aggregation.

indicators.name: GT13 Post-Exploitation Tool Execution
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: GreyNoise13 Post-Exploitation Tool Execution
id: 2b9a1c3d-e4f5-4a8b-9c0d-1e2f3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of Nmap or Chisel, which were used by the GreyNoise13 threat actor for reconnaissance and tunneling after compromising servers.
references:
  - https://www.cybersecuritydive.com/news/ai-enabled-campaign-targets-check-point-security-management-servers/875622/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-25
tags:
  - attack.t1046
  - attack.t1572
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\nmap.exe'
      - '\chisel.exe'
  condition: selection

indicators.name: Impacket Tool Command-Line Artifacts
indicators.pattern:
title: Impacket Tool Command-Line Artifacts
id: 8d7e6f5a-4b3c-4d2e-1f0a-9b8c7d6e5f4a
status: experimental
description: Detects command-line arguments related to Impacket tools (e.g., psexec.py, secretsdump.py), used by GreyNoise13 for lateral movement.
references:
  - https://www.cybersecuritydive.com/news/ai-enabled-campaign-targets-check-point-security-management-servers/875622/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-25
tags:
  - attack.t1021.002
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'impacket-'
  condition: selection

indicators.name: Potential Check Point Auth Bypass (CVE-2026-16232)
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Check Point Auth Bypass (CVE-2026-16232)
id: 5a4b3c2d-1e0f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: Detects anomalous login events in Check Point SmartConsole logs that may indicate an authentication bypass attempt related to CVE-2026-16232.
references:
  - https://www.cybersecuritydive.com/news/ai-enabled-campaign-targets-check-point-security-management-servers/875622/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-25
tags:
  - attack.t1190
level: critical
logsource:
  product: checkpoint
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection:
    keywords:
      - 'Anomalous login pattern consistent with CVE-2026-16232'
      - 'Authentication bypass successful'
  condition: selection
